tasks.title: Fix signup routing: remove URL-based view init and use pure conditional rendering
tasks.description:
1. WHAT: The QA agent could not find the 'Sign up' button on the login page because App.tsx initialises the `view` state using `window.location.pathname`, which can resolve to an unexpected value in test/hosted environments, causing the Signup view to render instead of Login on first load. The fix is to remove all URL-dependency from the routing and use pure React state-based conditional rendering.

2. READ FIRST: Read src/App.tsx (full file — focus on the `view` useState initialiser and the two `window.history.pushState` calls inside the JSX click handlers). Read src/components/Login.tsx and src/components/Signup.tsx to confirm prop interfaces are unchanged. Read src/App.test.tsx and src/components/Login.test.tsx to understand existing test coverage.

3. FILES:
   - MODIFY src/App.tsx — change the `view` useState initialiser from `() => window.location.pathname === '/signup' ? 'signup' : 'login'` to simply `'login'` (no lazy init needed). Remove the two `window.history.pushState(...)` calls inside the `onGoToSignup` and `onGoToLogin` click handler arrow functions — keep only the `setView(...)` call in each. No other changes to this file.
   - MODIFY src/App.test.tsx — audit existing tests; if any test asserts on URL pathname or relies on `window.location`, update or remove those assertions so tests reflect pure state-based routing.

4. APPROACH: The Login and Signup components are already correctly implemented with the 'Sign up' and 'Back to login' buttons present. Only App.tsx needs updating. Do NOT add react-router-dom or any external routing library. The fix is a one-line change to the useState default plus removal of the two pushState side-effects.

5. PATTERNS: The resulting App.tsx view logic should mirror simple conditional rendering: `useState<'login' | 'signup'>('login')` with `setView('signup')` / `setView('login')` as the only navigation mechanism — no URL side-effects.
acceptance_criteria: When the app first loads, the Sign In form is visible with email and password fields
A 'Sign up' button or link is visible below the Login submit button on the Sign In form
Clicking the 'Sign up' link replaces the Sign In form with the Sign Up form (email, password, confirm-password fields visible)
Clicking 'Back to login' on the Sign Up form returns to the Sign In form

tasks.title: Run full test suite to validate signup routing fix
tasks.description:
Run the complete Vitest test suite to confirm all existing tests pass after the App.tsx routing fix. Execute the following commands in order:
1. npx vitest run src/App.test.tsx
2. npx vitest run src/components/Login.test.tsx
3. npx vitest run src/components/Signup.test.tsx
4. npx vitest run src/auth/credentialStore.test.ts
5. npx tsc --noEmit
All commands must exit with code 0. Report any failures with the exact error output.
acceptance_criteria: npx vitest run src/App.test.tsx exits code 0 with all tests passing
npx vitest run src/components/Login.test.tsx exits code 0 with all tests passing
npx vitest run src/components/Signup.test.tsx exits code 0 with all tests passing
npx vitest run src/auth/credentialStore.test.ts exits code 0 with all tests passing
npx tsc --noEmit exits code 0 with no type errors
